thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Struggles For Footing In The Green, But Nasdaq Sets Fresh Intraday Peak

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Struggles For Footing In The Green, But Nasdaq Sets Fresh Intraday Peak
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer and Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch
Twitter, Apple, Mylan all stocks in focus for Tuesday
U.S. stock benchmarks fought for purchase in positive territory in Tuesday trade, but the Nasdaq secured an intraday all-time high, underscoring a resurgence in the sector that has been among the market's more influential.
What are markets doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 30 points, or 0.1%, to 24,784, while the S&P 500 index was up about a point, or less than 0.1%, at 2,748. The Nasdaq Composite Index climbed 18 points, or 0.2%, at 7,624, on track for its third straight up day after touching an intrasession record at 7,644.48, marking its first such record since March 13, according to FactSet data.
On Monday, the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-street-poised-for-higher-open-as-jobs-optimism-outweighs-trade-fears-2018-06-04) for the first time since March 12, rising 0.7%, to 7,606.46. The S&P 500 finished 0.5%, to 2,746.87, while, the Dow advanced 178.48 points, or 0.7%, to 24,813.69.
Read:Techs lead buyback boom, on track to put trillions back into investor hands (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-leads-stock-market-buyback-boom-with-companies-on-track-to-put-trillions-back-in-investor-hands-2018-06-04)
The small-capitalization oriented Russell 2000 index logged an intraday peak at 1,661.70, after closing at a fresh record on Tuesday, rising 0.3%, to 1,653.37.
See:Small caps offer stock-market leadership amid tumult (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/small-caps-offer-stock-market-leadership-amid-tumult-2018-06-02)
What was driving the market?
The market's gains were being fueled by the technology sector, given the advance for the Nasdaq, driven by some of the group's largest and most dominant companies, including Apple Inc., which saw its shares score a record on Monday, as details from its software-focused Worldwide Developers Conference emerged. A rise for Twitter Inc. shares, which were expected to be included in the S&P 500 index, also helped buoy enthusiasm for the technology and internet segment.
Tuesday's moves also come as Wall Street looks to regroup after recent upheaval triggered by political turmoil in Italy. More stability on that front could be in the offing, if the new Italian coalition government makes it past a confidence vote in parliament.
Investors appeared to be putting trade tensions aside, even after trade talks broke down between the U.S. and China over the weekend. But leaders of the Group of Seven nations will hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday, where tariffs and trade are likely to be discussed. This weekend's rebuke by G-7 finance ministers of the Trump administration's trade tariffs could add some stress to the gathering.
Read:Death knell for the G-7 may be at hand after hostile reaction to Trump tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/death-knell-for-the-g-7-may-be-at-hand-after-hostile-reaction-to-trump-tariffs-2018-06-04)
What are strategists saying?
"The fact of the matter is that investors are realizing that the tech sector is the sector they can count on for solid earnings growth," said Lindsey Bell, investment strategist at CFRA. Bell said that since the second quarter earnings-per-share growth for the S&P 500's tech sector has some in about 7 percentage points better that the broader market on average.
"Our view is that the current economic expansion and bull market has room to run and we aren't looking at the prospect of a recession starting until 2020 at the earliest," said Albert Brenner, director of asset allocation strategy at People's United Advisors.
Which stocks were in focus?
Mylan NV(MYL) shares surged 6.4% after the drugmaker received Food and Drug Administration approval (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mylan-rallies-on-fda-approval-of-biotech-drug-similar-to-amgens-2018-06-04) for a drug similar to one made by Amgen Inc.(AMGN).
Twitter Inc. (TWTR) shares jumped 5.4% after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the microblogging platform's stock would join the S&P 500 index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/twitter-shares-rise-on-announced-addition-to-sp-500-2018-06-04).
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) rose 0.8% and as the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech giant announced new augmented-reality development tools and software upgrades for all its products, along with a new Apple Watch at the company's developers' conference.
See:Apple's WWDC: Blocks on Facebook sharing s urprise, but no lift to $1 trillion market cap (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-wwdc-no-immediate-catalysts-to-get-to-1-trillion-market-cap-2018-06-04)
Starbucks Corp.(SBUX) slipped 2.2% after its executive chairman, Howard Schultz, said he would step down late Monday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/starbucks-chairman-howard-schultz-to-step-down-2018-06-04).
What's on the economic calendar?
The Institute for Supply Management services index rose to 58.6 in May from 56.8, while a reading of job openings rose to a fresh record in April, reaching 6.7 million after 6.63 million in March, the Labor Department said Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/job-openings-reach-new-record-in-april-2018-06-05).
Opinion:A new economic indicator is saying there is no sign of a U.S. recession (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-new-economic-indicator-is-saying-theres-no-sign-of-a-us-recession-2018-06-05)
See:MarketWatch's economic calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks finished mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-give-up-some-of-mondays-gains-2018-06-04), while the Stoxx Europe 600 index climbed as the tech sector hit a 17-year high (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-climb-as-tech-sector-hits-17-year-high-2018-06-05).
Crude oil reversed direction (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-claw-back-some-gains-as-global-production-worries-hover-2018-06-05), rising by 0.1% to $64.67 a barrel, after settling at the lowest level in nearly two months on Monday. Gold drifted lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-continues-to-languish-below-1300-2018-06-05) at $1,294.80 an ounce, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index was also steady (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-inches-up-as-nafta-comments-weigh-on-loonie-peso-2018-06-05) at 94.039.
